title: Per-tenant concurrency budgeter and softbuffer shedding for Dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short-lived concentrated request bursts from individual tenants that degrade tail latency for other tenants and trigger large autoscaler churn. Existing global admission/shaping layers are either too coarse (per-fleet token pools) or too aggressive (hard drops), which leads to avoidable SLA violations and customer support incidents.

Goal: Implement a per-tenant concurrency budgeting layer with a small in-memory softbuffer for transient bursts plus a predictive slowdown path. The feature aims to: (1) protect fleet-level tail latency and SLOs by preventing single-tenant burst collapse, (2) reduce autoscaler thrash by absorbing micro-bursts without scaling, and (3) provide graceful degradation (soft shedding + informative responses) rather than hard rejections where possible.

Design summary:
- Concurrency budgeter: Track an exponentially smoothed active-concurrency estimate per tenant (short window, ~10s) and assign a soft budget (concurrency credits) derived from the tenant's committed throughput + dynamic headroom allocation. Budgets are enforced at the per-ingress proxy before routing to model workers.
- Softbuffer: Each tenant gets a modest softbuffer (burst credits) that can be used to temporarily exceed the budget for sub-second spikes. Softbuffer consumption increases the tenant's smoothing factor and adds a short cooldown to avoid rapid repeated bursts.
- Predictive slowdown path: When budget + softbuffer are exhausted, instead of immediate hard drop, requests enter a lightweight in-proxy slowdown mode where request processing is delayed by a small randomized backoff and optional partial-response or cached-result fallback is attempted. Slowdown severity is proportional to overage and current fleet latency envelope.
- Metrics and telemetry: Expose per-tenant budget usage, softbuffer fill/consumption, slowdown entry rate, average added latency, and downstream SLO delta. Provide a simulation tool to replay historical ingress traces against the budgeter to tune parameters.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs. benefit: Adding per-tenant state increases memory and CPU overhead on the ingress tier; we cap state by LRU eviction and only track tenants with >1 req/s.
- Softbuffer sizing: Too large a buffer defeats isolation goals; too small yields frequent slowdowns. We opt for a conservative default (20% of committed concurrency, bounded by absolute cap) and surface a tenant-level knob in Dedicated configs.
- Predictive slowdown correctness: Introducing in-proxy delays inflates client-observed latency. We calibrate to keep added latency <50ms for 95% of slowdowns and provide a toggle to prefer cached partial results for latency-sensitive tenants.

Implementation phases:
1) Simulation + parameter sweep (local trace replay harness).
2) Ingress proxy MVP with read-only budget enforcement and per-tenant metrics (no slowdown path).
3) Slowdown path rollout behind feature flag + integration tests.
4) Canary on a small Dedicated pool -> evaluate SLO impact, autoscaler behavior, and cost metrics.
5) Full rollout and tenant opt-in knob in Console.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Initial architecture doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/concurrency-budgeter (internal). Requested feedback from runtime and infra teams.
2026-02-18 - Runtime team review: suggested moving smoothing/window logic into the ingress layer to avoid RPCs to control-plane; Rafael to prototype in ingress proxy.

2026-02-23 - Prototype completed: local harness replayed 48h of production ingress trace; preliminary results show 45% fewer autoscaler triggers for micro-bursts and <0.8% additional 95th latency impact when softbuffer enabled.
2026-02-28 - Security review kickoff: sending feature spec to security for potential information exposure from per-tenant metrics (no sensitive data expected).
2026-03-03 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/912 - MVP enforcement + metrics. Need infra approval for canary config.
2026-03-05 - QA notes: found race where eviction of tenant state during active cooldown resets cooldown timer incorrectly. Bug ticket created and assigned to Rafael (ENG-911005).
monitoring: alert:DBB-SlowdownSpike (sudden increase in slowdown entries > 200% baseline)
rollout_plan: Week 1: simulation & canary harness. Week 2: deploy ingress MVP to canary fleet (2 small Dedicated pools) with feature flag. Week 3: enable slowdown path for canary and run 72h verification. Week 4: incremental rollout by region and per-customer opt-in knob in Console. Full enablement only after SLO targets verified and no unexplained autoscaler regressions.
migration_notes: Existing tenants will default to 'legacy global shaping' until opt-in. Migration tool to compute recommended per-tenant budget from historical 7d QPS and peak concurrency will be added to Console. No downtime expected.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation harness reproduces >30% reduction in autoscaler micro-triggers on 7d production trace for typical SaaS tenants
Canary shows <1% increase in fleet 95th latency attributable to budgeter when softbuffer enabled
Feature flag allows immediate rollback with zero client-side changes
Per-tenant metrics are emitted and documented for SRE and customer success
